properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19 as part of the block-by-block plan reconciliation: found via a real-city-block coverage audit (src/block_fit.py load_blocks() matched against the OCII plan's blocks '7E'/'7W' label positions, which both resolve to the same coarse real-street-bounded block since no mapped internal street separates them) as a genuinely untracked real building. Its own Assessor lot (blklot 8711227, a standalone parcel recorded 2012) is distinct from the neighboring already-tracked buildings (Strata, Madrone) -- confirmed via the DataSF Assessor tax roll API rather than assumed from proximity. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: identifying the true '7W' block (Five88, blklot 8711226, added separately) exposed a 117 sq m overlap between this building's real DataSF footprint and Five88's real Assessor parcel boundary at their shared property line -- trimmed via geom.difference() against the Five88 parcel, same pattern as this project's other real-parcel-vs-real-footprint trims (e.g. Chase Center Parking Garage vs Uber Mission Bay 2). CONFIRMED 2026-09-19: found an independent primary-adjacent source explicitly naming this 'Block 7 East' -- Citizen Portal's report on OCII's own March 18 commission meeting, which approved CEQA findings and the combined basic concept/schematic design for 'Family House's institutional building on Block 7 East in Mission Bay South' (80 guest rooms, 42 parking spaces, architect Richard Stacy), closing the citation gap flagged when this record was first added.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed DataSF building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate; trimmed 117 sq m at the shared boundary with the neighboring Five88 parcel (blklot 8711226) -- see digitization_method.
properties.notes: 5-story, 80-room nonprofit 'home away from home' for families of children being treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital -- free lodging, low-income-qualified, run by the 501(c)(3) Family House, Inc. (founded 1981). Opened at this Mission Bay location in 2016 after moving from an earlier Judah St. building; accommodates up to 250 people/night, serves 3,000+ families/year. Assessor's welfare exemption on the parcel matches its nonprofit operation.
